correctness.rationale: The published matrix quotient and geometric irreducible-characteristic criterion hold for all finite fields. In characteristic 3, trace descends and the negative linear coefficient on its kernel equals a well-defined quadratic form. Irreducibility forces this coefficient to be a nonzero square through the additive-cubic permutation contradiction. A binary quadratic form on any 2D odd-order finite-field space must attain zero or a nonsquare, by diagonalization and surjectivity of the quadratic-extension norm. Hence there is no smooth tracezero plane and no smooth net; a smooth pencil has exactly one tracezero member. The cubic field k[A] constructs a pencil through every smooth member for every q=3^r. The verifier reproduced F9 quadratic and F3 pencil tests but is not used as proof for arbitrary exponents.
